newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices rise at week's sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices rise at week's sales.

text.p: Australian wool prices rose by about three percent when sales resumed this week in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle after the Christmas recess, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The eastern market indicator rose by 16 cents to 584 cents a kg clean, while the western indicator rose 17 cents to 559 cents a kg.
A total of 73,836 bales were offered, which was about 60,000 bales less than that of the last auction before Christmas.
The trade bought 94 percent, with a pass-in rate of six percent.
Wool International said trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with good support from Taiwanese buyers and most sectors of the trade.

"Indications of new Chinese business, stimulated by improved buyer confidence and the weaker Australian dollar which fell over a cent on Wednesday to US$0.7775, will also provide the market with good support and declinging wool available from Wool International, who are well in advance completing sales for the March quarter, will also assist prices," Wesfarmers said.
Wool International said its stockpile totalled 1.93 million bales at January 9.
